key_insight: Standardizing prostate cancer EHR data to OMOP, then adding NLP and PSA-based rules, markedly improved capture of diagnosis, pathology, treatment, and recurrence information.
clinical_relevance: This approach could make real-world prostate cancer data more complete and research-ready, while also helping identify missing or inconsistent registry records.
method: Built an OMOP CDM v5.4 pipeline from UTMB Epic EHR data for registry-identified prostate cancer cases (2010–2021).
Compared OMOP data quality with cancer registry records using agreement metrics.
Applied NLP to extract PSA, Gleason score, and stage from clinical text, plus PSA-based algorithms for missing treatment and biochemical recurrence.
evidence_signal: From 815 analytic cases, 700 (85.9%) were complete and concordant with the cancer registry; PSA agreement was excellent, and NLP substantially improved sparse Gleason/stage capture.
watch_item: Performance depends on local EHR structure, text quality, and PSA data availability, so the workflow may need site-specific validation before broader use.
paper_title: Developing an OMOP-Standardized Prostate Cancer Database and Improving Data Quality Using NLP and PSA-Based Algorithms
